items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Old man named Paul Rose gave me my little start on music.

ctx.x: Were you in the leader or something?

Well, no, I just did all the work. We didn't have no leader. I was holding the band up. I said, they didn't give me the six bits. How old were you then, Doc? Well, I said I was sixteen. We was young. See, the old ones give us the band. They got new instruments. And everybody that had anybody relation to them, well, they just give them the instrument, they took the new instrument. So I didn't know quite in the band, so they just give me the bass drum. And I played it. Started to tune with them horns and I could…

He did now, too. Some of these people weren't here last night when you were telling about your life. That was in Raceland? Raceland, yeah. When were you born? What was your birthday? 1894. The birthday is, uh... Exactly. December 9th. December. December 9th. December 9th. December 9th. Yeah. Right before Christmas. Yeah. Been a good while back. Yeah. Ninety- 1894. That's right.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: They were strictly musicians like Paul Rose and Mike Taylor, Spencer Taylor's name.

ctx.x: What about out in the country? Did they play trumpet pretty much the same as in the city? Did they use the same tricks?

Well, not them days. They didn't. They were strictly musicians like Paul Rose and Mike Taylor, Spencer Taylor's name. They put that music up there and just played parades and things. They didn't play no dance music. They played parades and things. What about half-elvin? Did they do that much in those days?
Well, I did that a lot. Tell me that comes from King Oliver. Tell me King Oliver first one did that.
